forces.label: Resilience across connected services
forces.what: Cyber risk crosses markets; the exposure belongs to a specific service and entity.
forces.why: Operational dependencies can transmit disruption across suppliers, channels and critical services.
forces.next: Ask which critical service, recovery objective and supplier dependency needs customer validation.
forces.counter: Aggregate threat evidence does not establish an enterprise incident, control weakness or external services gap.

forces.label: UK cyber reform: a proposal, not a duty
forces.what: Parliamentary stages still show consideration of Lords amendments pending at this review.
forces.why: Possible changes merit monitoring; proposal wording cannot prove current non-compliance.
forces.next: Recheck parliamentary status and final entity/activity scope before making a legal applicability claim.
forces.counter: No Royal Assent or final enterprise applicability is established by this reviewed passage.

forces.label: Social value in covered UK tenders
forces.what: From 1 January 2027, PPN 026 covers specified central-government procurements of £1m or more, inclusive of VAT; framework and transition rules matter.
forces.why: This can affect bid design and delivery commitments; it need not create a standalone revenue opportunity.
forces.next: Identify the contracting authority, tender notice date, total contract value, framework and actual award criteria.
forces.counter: Private utilities and primarily overseas delivery are excluded; transitions and framework/call-off rules require review. French procurements do not inherit this policy.

forces.label: UK listed-issuer sustainability reporting
forces.what: FCA final rules introduce comply-or-explain UK SRS reporting for specified listing categories, for accounting periods starting from 1 January 2027.
forces.why: Reporting data, controls and assurance may need investigation; group location does not determine scope.
forces.next: Verify exact issuer, listing category, accounting period and transitional relief before discussing a work package.
forces.counter: First reporting is in 2028; reliefs and scope matter. Existing internal teams or advisers may already cover the work.

forces.label: France: reporting law and transposition differ
forces.what: ESMA describes the EU Omnibus amendment as in force, while French guidance distinguishes national transposition.
forces.why: EU adoption, national effective rules and an entity’s reporting wave are separate questions.
forces.next: Check the current French implementing text, reporting wave and exact legal entity; do not apply proposed thresholds early.
forces.counter: French guidance last checked texts on 2 September 2026; this is not a complete current-law or enterprise applicability determination.

limitations: Only UK/France reference contexts are researched; blank markets are unresearched, not safe or compliant.
No legal-entity identity, parent/subsidiary footprint, buying authority, budget or supplier demand is verified by this prototype.
Industry archetypes are reused; French supplier, competition and operating-market facts are not populated.
Seller offering is an ephemeral declared relevance filter, not a private profile, territorial permission or customer qualification.
